judgment_text:
PRAYER : - To issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate Writ, or order or direction, more in the form of Writ, direct the respondents 1 to 6 to permit the petitioner to do pooja (Sami Aaduthal and Kuri Solluthal) in the above said temple, namely, Arulmigu Sree Pathala Kaliamman Kovil, at Kadaladi Village, Kadaladi Taluk, Ramanathapuram District, in the temple festival scheduled to be held on 14-4-2026 to 21-4-2026 and consequently direct the respondents 2 and 5 to provide necessary police protection to the petitioner and 120 family members for offering worship in the temple.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

L. Victoria Gowri, J.:— This Writ Petition is filed seeking to issue a writ of mandamus, directing the respondents 1 to 6 to permit the petitioner to do pooja (Sami Aaduthal and Kuri Solluthal) in the above said temple, namely, Arulmigu Sree Pathala Kaliamman Kovil, at Kadaladi Village, Kadaladi Taluk, Ramanathapuram District, in the temple festival scheduled to be held on 14-4-2026 to 21-4-2026 and consequently direct the respondents 2 and 5 to provide necessary police protection to the petitioner and 120 family members for offering worship in the temple.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that he is the Poojari of the temple, namely, Arulmigu Sree Pathala Kaliamman Kovil, at Kadaladi Village, Kadaladi Taluk, Ramanathapuram District, which belongs to 7 villagers, namely, Kannan Paduvan, Sirukudi, Pookulam, Oorivayal, Karunkulam, Kolikulam and Kolunthurai. Every Tamil month of Chithirai, Chitrai festival would be conducted by the villagers of all the seven villages for 7 days and the same is scheduled to be held from 14-4-2026 to 21-4-2026. The petitioner's father, namely, Ramaswamy, son of Veeraputhiran was the temple poojari for the past 30 years and he passed away on 6-1-2026. Since his demise, the petitioner had taken the role of Poojari of the temple following the customs of Kurisolluthal and Sami Aaduthal.

3. While so, the private respondents residing in other villages, more particularly 7 to 9th respondents, are hindering the petitioner from continuing his Poojariship and also excommunicated 120 family members belonging to Scheduled Caste community from participating in the scheduled temple festival, including the petitioner. In this regard, on 6-4-2026, the petitioner made a representation to the official respondents 1 to 6 to permit the petitioner to do pooja in the temple and also to facilitate the excommunicated 120 family members to participate in the said temple festival. Since the same is not considered, this petition is filed.

4. The learned government advocate drew my attention to the order passed by this Court in WP Crl(MD) No. 1705 of 2026, filed by one Kalicharan in which this Court had directed the Revenue Authority to conduct a peace committee and thereafter facilitate the commencement of the scheduled temple festival. Since already an order has been passed in this regard by this Court in WP Crl(MD) No. 1705 of 2026, this writ petition is also filed for a similar relief with respect to the same temple.

5. In view of the submissions made by either side, the third respondent is directed to conclude the peace committee between the petitioner faction and the 7th to 9th respondent faction before 12-4-2026.

6. The learned counsel for the private respondents 7 to 9 categorically contended that there is no question of excommunicating any person from participating in the temple festival and the petitioner's narrative as if the private respondents have excommunicated 120 families from participating in the temple festival, is absolutely false and they will not hinder any person from participating in the temple festival.

7. Heard either sides and carefully perused the materials available on record.

8. Since it is seen that the representation given by the petitioner before the second respondent has already been forwarded to the fifth respondent and due summons have been issued by the fifth respondent to the respective parties to appear before them on 10-4-2026, the fifth respondent is directed to forthwith forward the same before the third respondent. The third respondent, on receipt of the same, is directed to conduct a peace committee between the petitioner faction and the rival factions and facilitate the conduct of the temple festival as scheduled from 14-4-2026 to 21-4-2026, by ensuring that none of the person of either faction, is excommunicated or prevented from participating in any of the connected functions and ceremonies of the scheduled temple festival. It is also made made clear that none of the person should seek any first honour during the temple festival.

9. With the above direction, this Writ Petition is disposed of. No costs.
